preamble: Diphthongization of [u] (here the long vowel [uː]) to the falling diphthong [ou̯]. In Czech, Old Czech long ú became ou in the 15th and 16th centuries: múka /ˈmuːka/ > mouka [ˈmou̯ka] 'flour', súd /ˈsuːd/ > soud [ˈsou̯t] 'court', and the instrumental ending -ú became -ou (vranú > vranou 'crow'). Sixteenth-century spelling wrote the new diphthong au. At the start of a word the change was used only in lower-prestige or specialised styles, and the standard language keeps ú there.

examples.note: Likewise silú > silou 'strength' (instrumental). The diphthongization began in the Hussite period (15th century) and was established in the 16th, when it was still written au.

sources: Wikipedia contributors (2026). History of the Czech language. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_the_Czech_language
